validator.authorize.keyCodes.label: Validator key
validator.authorize.stop.heading: Stop this account's keys
validator.authorize.stop.body: No key will sign for this account from the day it counts.
validator.authorize.keys.unmarked.one: One key here isn't marked as this validator's. It holds {percent} of this account's authorization. Sign only if you know it, for example as the key of your other computer.
validator.authorize.keys.unmarked.other: {count} keys here aren't marked as this validator's. Together they hold {percent} of this account's authorization. Sign only if you know each of them, for example as the keys of your other computers.
validator.authorize.version.label: Authorization
validator.authorize.version.implausible: Authorization #{version} is far above the number a validator drafts, which is one above the account's last authorization. A later authorization needs a larger number still. Don't sign unless you expected this number.
validator.authorize.signed.keys.one: This signature authorizes the key {codes} for {account}, as authorization #{version}.
validator.authorize.signed.keys.other: This signature authorizes the keys {codes} for {account}, as authorization #{version}.
validator.authorize.signed.stop: This signature stops every key of {account}, as authorization #{version}.
validator.authorize.signed.network.test: It counts only on the test network it was made for.
validator.authorize.signature.heading: Copy the signature
validator.authorize.signature.instructio: Paste it into your validator's Authorize step, in the box for the signature.
validator.authorize.signature.selectToCo: Select the text and copy it.
validator.authorize.page.title: Authorize your validator
validator.authorize.intro.body: Your wallet signs one message that lets the 6529 Validator on your computer sign for this account. It costs no gas and moves nothing.
validator.authorize.intro.check: Check that your validator's screen shows the same key code. If it doesn't, or someone sent you this link, stop here.
validator.authorize.wallet.safe: A vault such as a Safe can't sign in this version. Connect the ordinary wallet you use on 6529.io.
validator.authorize.wallet.wrong: Connect {expected}, the wallet your validator asked for. This wallet is {connected}.
validator.authorize.sign.mismatch: This signature isn't from {expected}. Your validator won't take it.
validator.authorize.sign.rejected: You cancelled in your wallet. Nothing was signed.
validator.authorize.sign.failed: Your wallet didn't sign. Try again.
validator.authorize.sign.note.keys: Your wallet shows the same words. Each key's public key ends in its code. Signing costs no gas.
validator.authorize.sign.note.stop: Your wallet shows the same words. Signing costs no gas.
validator.authorize.problems.heading: Don't sign this. It isn't a 6529 Validator authorization.
validator.authorize.link.bad: This link is incomplete or damaged. Scan the code again, or copy the link again from your validator.
validator.authorize.noLink.heading: Sign for your validator on your phone
validator.authorize.noLink.body: This page lets the wallet on your phone authorize a 6529 Validator that runs on your computer. Your wallet signs one message. It costs no gas and moves nothing.
validator.authorize.noLink.step.open: On your computer, open 6529 Validator and go to Authorize, or to Keys, then Add a computer.
validator.authorize.noLink.step.address: Choose your phone as the wallet, and paste its address.
validator.authorize.noLink.step.scan: Scan the code it shows with your phone, or open its link here.
validator.authorize.noLink.step.sign: Sign here, then paste the signature into your validator.
validator.authorize.noLink.check: Sign only if the key code on this page matches the one on your computer.
validator.authorize.noLink.about: {link} Read about it and download it there.
